title: Freeze the Clock
prompt: Implement greeting(name, now=None) returning 'Good morning, <name>!' for hours 5-11, 'Good afternoon' for 12-17, 'Good evening' otherwise. now is a datetime; default to datetime.now(). Then write TestGreeting that patches the clock (patch the module-level datetime or inject fixed datetimes via now=) to test all three bands. Assign to SUITE_TEST.
boilerplate:
import unittest
from datetime import datetime

def greeting(name, now=None):
    pass

class TestGreeting(unittest.TestCase):
    pass

SUITE_TEST = None

tests.name: bands work with injected times
tests.code:
from datetime import datetime
assert greeting('An', datetime(2026, 1, 1, 8)) == 'Good morning, An!'
assert greeting('An', datetime(2026, 1, 1, 14)) == 'Good afternoon, An!'
assert greeting('An', datetime(2026, 1, 1, 22)) == 'Good evening, An!'
tests.hint: Branch on now.hour when now is provided.

tests.name: default path uses real clock
tests.code:
g = greeting('An')
assert g.startswith(('Good morning', 'Good afternoon', 'Good evening'))

tests.name: all three bands tested
